title: Chicken salad with broad beans and asparagus

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain staple such as Dijon mustard and olive oil, with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Chicken breasts, asparagus, broad beans, radishes, watercress and tarragon are all everyday supermarket lines in late May.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a frying pan, a saucepan and a small bowl, and the techniques are simple frying, boiling and whisking.

works.reason: Halved breasts fried for 4 to 5 minutes a side will cook through, 3 minutes suits the beans and asparagus, and 1kg of pods with three breasts makes a fair lunch for four.

honest_times.reason: Podding 1kg of beans while the chicken fries, plus trimming, slicing and making the dressing, fits about 18 active minutes, and 12 minutes covers the frying and boiling.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm salad of fresh podded broad beans with asparagus and radishes suits late May, and the beans are a main component, not a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English instructions that a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a satisfying protein and vegetable lunch of real food that a family would happily eat.
